profile.entities: Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Ltd.; Tiller Therapeutics

bull_bear.body: The company is focused on allocating capital efficiently, with a focus on investing in high-priority programs and reducing costs where possible.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: The company faces significant risks, including the risk of clinical trial failure and the risk of regulatory delays.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's focus on synthetic lethality and targeted therapies positions it well for future growth, with a strong pipeline of products in development.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Early development has been funded using promoter-backed debt, cumulatively $45 million-plus as of Q2 FY'26.
- The company says it needs significant additional resources and is finalising a funding plan to extend the cash window to FY'28, expected to complete in the first half of this calendar year.
- Capital discipline on vodobatinib: progressing second-line CML now requires a costlier late-stage study with an active comparator, and with limited large-pharma licensing interest SPARC may prefer partners/investors using alternative structures; a final decision on the programme's future is expected fairly soon.
- The SCO-155 NewCo structure is presented as the template: SPARC and UCSF signed a binding Letter of Intent with Tiller Therapeutics, which obtains exclusive global rights while SPARC is eligible for significant equity of Tiller; Tiller raised pre-seed capital in 2025 and is raising priced external seed capital.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Part of the Sun Pharma group, with ongoing related-party dealings (R&D services, corporate guarantee, funding) with group entities such as Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited, Sun Pharma Laboratories Limited, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Inc., and Shanghvi Finance Private Limited
- Demonstrated ability to secure USFDA regulatory milestones — granted a Priority Review Voucher (PRV) for Sezaby® by the USFDA on February 3, 2026, subsequently sold for USD 195 million
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Clinical and scientific execution risk — Pharmaceutical R&D involves inherent uncertainty exploring novel scientific pathways; SPARC faces variability in clinical outcomes and scientific intricacies in discovering and advancing novel therapeutic candidates
- Evolving regulatory requirements — SPARC operates amid evolving and increasingly stringent regulatory requirements and shifting global regulatory and policy frameworks, which affect its research and development programs
- Intellectual property protection dependency — The Company's success depends on strong intellectual property protection in a highly dynamic environment
- Financial sustainability tied to R&D outcomes and macro factors — Financial sustainability remains closely linked to the progress and outcomes of research programs, and can be influenced by external macroeconomic factors such as currency movements, interest rate fluctuations, and geopolitical developments
- Supply chain and specialised equipment availability — Potential supply chain disruptions affecting availability of critical materials and specialized equipment may impact development timelines
- Third-party manufacturing/regulatory compliance risk — For its licensed-out asset PDP-716, the partner (Ocuvex Therapeutics) received a Complete Response Letter from the FDA due to inspection findings at a third-party API manufacturing facility, and the finished-product manufacturing site continues to face compliance issues requiring remediation — illustrating dependence on third-party manufacturing and regulatory compliance for commercialised/out-licensed programs
- Technological pace-of-change risk — The Company must keep pace with rapid technological advancements in a highly dynamic R&D environment
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The company's oncology segment is focused on developing targeted therapies, including ADCs and bispecific antibodies, while the immunology segment is focused on developing novel treatments for autoimmune diseases.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- The reset is built on three pillars: narrowing therapeutic focus to oncology and immunology and executing on two programs nearing clinic; reducing the burden of clinical risk within SPARC via alternative structures like NewCos; and converting short-term cash options while optimising the cost structure.
- Preclinical portfolio is deliberately consolidated into three tightly defined themes: targeted delivery to tumours (antibody- or synthetic small-molecule-ligand mediated), synthetic lethality, and dermatology autoimmune disorders; management says it exited neurodegeneration almost completely.
- Management frames the MUC1-SEA epitope approach as unique: SBO-154 binds the alpha-beta junction rather than the VNTR region, which undergoes proteolytic cleavage and creates a peripheral sink; plasma samples of cancer patients showed significantly lower alpha-beta subunit levels than VNTR.
- Management's own balance caveat: 'ours is an early-stage portfolio with key assets yet to have even early clinical proof of concept. So investors who want to review this portfolio need to approach this with probability-adjusted view to valuation.'
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [PRV] The district court of the District of Columbia ruled the agency's decision to deny the pediatric rare disease voucher was contrary to law; subject to a possible appeal (window expiring end-January), SPARC expects to receive a voucher, with PRV transaction values going north of $100 million and a positive outcome described as potentially 'transformational'.
- [Orphan exclusivity] SPARC's Citizen Petition seeking removal of DESI phenobarbital formulations (indicated for neonatal seizures, containing toxic alcohol-based excipients) remains under review, with the agency indicating it needs more time.
- [Partner risk - PDP-716] The once-a-day brimonidine formulation was licensed to Visiox Pharma, since bought out by Ocuvex Therapeutics; the original NDA got a complete response letter due to the third-party API vendor's OAI status, and although resubmission is complete, the finished product manufacturing site has compliance issues requiring remediation and third-party sites are being qualified.
- [Regulatory relief] For SCD-153, DCGI approved a protocol amendment (solution to foam formulation, revised hair-loss cutoff) and waived the condition requiring CDSCO review before cohort 2, allowing an independent DSMB to open subsequent cohorts.

outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: The company has a strong pipeline of products in development, with multiple catalysts expected in the short term.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: The company has significant growth optionality, with multiple products in development and a strong pipeline of future catalysts.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Narrowed therapeutic emphasis to oncology and immunology, two of the fastest-growing areas, driven by advances in modalities such as ADCs, CGT and CAR-T therapies
- Building a modular, 'plug-and-play' biologics platform anchored on an anti-MUC1 antibody to enable rapid target integration and scalable development
- Three tightly defined strategic themes: targeted multi-modal cancer therapeutics (ADCs, bispecifics, ISACs, SMDCs, T-cell engagers); DNA Damage Response (DDR) pathway inhibitors for synthetic lethality; and dermatology/autoimmune therapies focused on non-JAK pathways
- Repositioned pipeline around two advanced assets: a differentiated ADC for select solid tumors and a novel immunology pathway asset in derma autoimmune
- Explored alternative business structures such as asset-specific NewCos to reduce the burden of clinical risk within SPARC, e.g., formation of Tiller Therapeutics to advance the SCO-155 SMDC program
- Cost optimisation: rationalised US footprint and streamlined operations, and consolidated its lab network from four centres to two, to reduce manpower cost
- Prudent financial management with continued cost discipline, active expense monitoring and prioritisation of high-return investments; used non-dilutive PRV-sale proceeds to strengthen balance sheet flexibility while minimising shareholder dilution
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body:
- Pipeline increasingly aligned with global biopharma value drivers — targeted biologics, precision oncology and next-generation combination therapies — areas attracting strong industry and investor interest
- Synthetic lethality strategy targets key drivers of PARP resistance, described as a well-recognised and commercially relevant oncology challenge, positioning assets in a high-demand segment complementing existing standards of care
- Dermatology/autoimmune focus targets CD8+ T-cell driven disorders where current treatment options are largely limited to oral or topical JAK inhibitors, an area management sees as underserved
- Sezaby (phenobarbital sodium injection for neonatal seizures) — FDA approved; associated Priority Review Voucher granted following favourable court ruling and subsequently sold
- SPARC-121 (previously SCD-153, for Alopecia Areata) — completed Phase 1a SAD study; Phase 1b MAD study actively recruiting patients with an interim readout expected in Q3 FY2026-27; also being explored in Vitiligo, with a Phase 1b proof-of-concept protocol submitted to the DCGI
- SPARC-122 (previously SBO-154, anti-MUC1 ADC for multiple tumour types) — Phase 1a dose-escalation study for solid tumors actively enrolling at 11 sites across the US, Australia and India; Phase 1b dose-expansion study planned in ER+ HER2-ve breast cancer, lung cancer and ovarian cancer once Phase 1a completes
- PDP-716 (Brimonidine formulation for open-angle glaucoma) — licensed to Visiox Pharma, rights now held by Ocuvex Therapeutics after buyout; NDA resubmission completed following a Complete Response Letter, though the finished-product manufacturing site faces compliance issues requiring remediation; SPARC assisting in qualifying alternate third-party manufacturing sites
- Tiller Therapeutics — an asset-specific NewCo formed to advance the SCO-155 Small Molecule Drug Conjugate (SMDC) program for metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer (mCRPC)
